title: New Era PH embracing homegrown communities as a global brand
summary: Since launching locally in 2015, New Era PH has become a staple of local street culture. To support their growing online store, they integrated PayMongo for automated settlements and built-in fraud protection. Discover how fintech helps this heritage brand scale securely.
body_markdown:
Long before New Era opened its first store in the Philippines, its caps were already being worn here. The fitted silhouettes and flat brims the brand is known for internationally had already found their way into the country's hip-hop and street culture scene by the early 2000s. When the global brand finally arrived, it wasn't introducing something *new* , but catching up to a market that had already shown interest.


"There's already an existing market for people who are into Western hip-hop and street culture here — way back, early 2000s to the 2010s," says Robert Murillo, e-commerce head of New Era Philippines.


The decision to bring the brand into the country, he says, was never about creating demand – it was about meeting it.


## **Local Twist on a Global Brand**


New Era Philippines is operated locally by a retailer and distributor that had already spent decades in the Philippine market before New Era arrived. That local trust is part of why, when the brand opened its first Philippine store in 2015, it didn't have to build an audience from zero. Last year, New Era marked ten years in the country — what the brand itself now calls less a milestone than "a movement."


In that decade, the brand grew, in its own words, from "a cap destination to a full-blown lifestyle brand, bringing together sport, fashion, and street culture." It leaned on everything the global name already had — decades of licensing with the NBA, NFL, and MLB, plus partnerships across music, entertainment, and more recently motorsports — and blended that into a culture that was already taking shape locally.


On the ground, that meant building relationships with homegrown names: rapper Gloc-9, visual artists like BenCab and the Secret Fresh collective, tattoo artist Whang-Od, rock band Kamikazee, and a collection honoring the late Francis Magalona, a foundational figure in Philippine hip-hop.


"We've collaborated successfully with a lot of artists and influencers over the years, and seeing them treat New Era as something that's already part of the culture — not a replacement for it — is what makes our mission feel like it's coming to life," Murillo says. The brand describes itself as "a badge of identity for cap collectors, culture carriers, and creatives alike" — and despite being a licensed outpost of a global name, the team talks about its Philippine identity as fundamentally homegrown, shaped by the community that choses to wear it.

## **The Right Fit**


Payments is one of the quieter parts of a retail business, but it demands constant attention. Reconciling a sale used to mean checking it by hand — cross-referencing the company's own records against a third-party payment system, transaction by transaction. "Before, we did that manually — checking both our own system and the third-party payment system by hand," Murillo says. "It was so time-consuming." And when a shipment ran late, the team couldn't always explain why — a delay rooted in back-end reconciliation isn't something a customer waiting on a package wants to hear about.


There was also the matter of brand trust. New Era PH had worked with a number of different providers before settling into a more dependable setup — and in an e-commerce business moving real volume, every provider swap carries its own fraud and settlement risk.


## **Future-Proofing Systems**


New Era PH's e-commerce runs on Shopify, and the team found that PayMongo’s plugin provides less friction within their operations. "Our e-commerce is hosted on Shopify, and PayMongo has that seamless API integration ready to go," Murillo says. "They're really system-ready for the future." The same setup, he notes, extends to Magento and WooCommerce — useful insurance for a brand that may need to move platforms as it scales.


The bigger shift was in reliability. "We weren't using PayMongo at first — we were using a lot of different payment partners," Murillo recalls. "Then we found PayMongo to be a valuable resource during the pandemic. We haven’t had any concerns with settlements and payments. So far, it's been 100% good in terms of settling finances, both with the business and with our customers."


Six to seven years into the relationship, that track record is the detail he keeps coming back to.


Security was the other half of the equation. "They \[PayMongo\] understand the market — they understand that there are frauds, there are stolen cards out there," Murillo says. "So they made sure they have secure payments in place, with a lot of quality checks on every customer's payment, aside from just OTP verification. It's a wider web of checks to ensure the security of every payment."


The numbers back it up: Murillo estimates that fraud flags, once a real concern, have dropped to roughly half a transaction out of every ten processed. "No one's perfect," he says, "but it's about as close to zero as it gets."


What used to live in spreadsheets now lives in one dashboard. Instead of manually checking transactions against a separate payment system, New Era PH's team can see everything — settlements, flagged transactions, payment status — in a single place. It's a small operational change that adds up: less time spent reconciling by hand means more time spent on the parts of the job that actually require a growth mindset.


## **Growing with the Culture**


There's a throughline between how New Era PH talks about its brand and how Murillo talks about the business behind it. Neither is interested in force. "People don't want to feel trapped into wearing one certain thing," Murillo says of the culture New Era serves. "I wear what I wear. I can be what I can be." The brand's role, as he sees it, is to supplement a culture that's already moving — supplying the caps and collaborations that let people express an identity they're already building, rather than dictating what that identity should look like.


That same instinct — build around what's already there instead of working against it — is what Murillo values in a payment partner, too. A system that settles reliably, catches fraud without creating friction for the customer, and plugs into the e-commerce platform a brand already runs on doesn't ask a company to change how it operates. It just clears the obstacles out of the way.


For a brand whose entire job is reading and responding to culture in real time, that's not a small thing — it's time and attention that would otherwise go into chasing down a missed settlement or a manual fraud check, freed up for the actual work of staying relevant.


## **An Evolving, New Era**


Murillo's outlook for the brand over the next five years reads like a continuation of everything that's gotten it here. "The culture is evolving so fast now," he says. "What I hope for is more of a multitude of subcultures emerging — and I think the brand is ready for it." He points to how New Era's designs already shift meaningfully year over year, and how its collaborations, local and global alike, keep expanding the list of communities it serves.


"We're still staying true to who we are," he adds. "That's already proven itself over the decades."


Asked for one piece of advice for other business owners, Murillo doesn't talk about product or marketing tactics. He talks about posture.


"Have the push and drive to be part of your consumers," he says. "It's not just about scaling the business — growth and community go hand in hand. You don't make the market come to you; you grow with it. Let the people speak, and let yourself hear them out."


It's the same principle that's carried New Era from a single store in 2015 to a homegrown name in Philippine streetwear — and, on the back end, the same principle that's kept its payments running quietly enough that nobody has to question it at all.


*New Era Philippines is a PayMongo merchant based in the Philippines, operating the local retail and e-commerce business of the global headwear and lifestyle brand New Era Cap Co. Shop the brand and follow its story at neweracap.ph and across its social platforms.*
